'''Draymond Green''' (born March 4, 1990) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State University]]. He plays the [[forward (basketball)|forward]] position.

==High School==
In high school, he led the Saginaw Trojans to two state championships. During his high school career, he averaged 20 points, 13 rebounds, and 2 blocked shots a game. His high school team recorded a 27-1 record and was ranked number 4 in the [[USA Today]] national high school rankings.<ref>http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/green_draymond00.html</ref> Coming out of high school, he was recruited by [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].<ref>http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/player/news?id=49155&_slug_=draymond-green&action=login&appRedirect=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/player/news%3fid%3d49155%26_slug_%3ddraymond-green</ref>

==College==
Originally having committed to Kentucky, Green eventually decided to play for [[Tom Izzo]] and the Michigan State Spartans. During the regular season of his freshman year (2008-09), Green came off the bench, averaging 3.3 points per game and 3.3 rebounds per game. But Green made significant contributions as a freshman during the team's run to the championship game in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]].  During his [[sophomore]] year (2009-10), he would win the [[Big Ten]] [[sixth man]] of the year award, averaging 9.9 points and 7.7 [[rebounds]] per game.<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=41760</ref> During his junior year (2010-11), Green averaged 12.6 points per game and 8.6 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Draymond Green  #23  F|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=41760|accessdate=24 March 2011}}</ref> On February 10, 2011, Green became the third player in Michigan State Men's basketball history to record a [[triple-double]], joining [[Charlie Bell (basketball)|Charlie Bell]] and [[Magic Johnson]].<ref name="State News">{{cite web|last=Vannini|first=Chris|title=Green’s triple-double sparks Spartan win, 75-57|url=http://www.statenews.com/index.php/article/2011/02/mbb.p1a.021111|accessdate=24 March 2011}}</ref> In the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] he recorded his second triple-double of the season and the eleventh in NCAA tournament history in the loss against [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6231466</ref>

As a senior (2011-12 season), Green captained the Spartans to a regular season Big Ten Championship, followed by a Big Ten Tournament Championship. <ref>http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Big_Ten_Conference_men%27s_basketball_season</ref>  The 2011-12 squad compiled a regular season 24-7 record and a 13-5 mark in Big Ten play, good for the team's 13th conference title and the third in the previous four years.<ref>http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Big_Ten_Conference_men%27s_basketball_season</ref>    Green was named Big Ten Men's Basketball Player of the week four times during the 2012 season; no other Spartan in history has won the award more than three times in a single season.  <ref>http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022112aaa.html</ref>  On March 5, 2012, Green was named Big Ten Player of the Year by the coaches and media and was a unanimous first-team All-Big Ten selection. <ref>http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030512aad.html</ref>  On March 10, 2012, Draymond passed Johnny Green as the second all-time rebounding leader at MSU, finishing the game with 1046 career rebounds<ref name=ESPN>{{cite web|title=Draymond Green carries No. 8 Spartans into first Big Ten finale since 2000|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320700127|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=3/13/12}}</ref> .  On March 16th, 2012, Draymond recorded his third career triple double against LIU-Brooklyn<ref>http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=320760127</ref> in the second round of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]] joining [[Oscar Robertson]] and [[Magic Johnson]] as just the third player in NCAA history to have 2 career triple doubles in the NCAA tournament.  On March 22, 2012, in a disappointing loss to Louisville, Green collected 16 rebounds, bringing him to 1,095 career rebounds.<ref>http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/41760/draymond-green</ref>  He now holds first place for total career rebounds in Michigan State history, 3 ahead of former record holder [[Greg Kelser]].
